text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ALL NEWSPAPERS

- President Suleyman Demirel of Turkey arrived on his first official visit in Latvia. Demirel voiced Turkey's support for Latvia's efforts to join NATO and the EU. At the same time Demirel expressed regret that the two countries still may not sign a free trade agreement.

- Parliament approved Talavs Jundzis as new defence minister. Jundzis, 46, is head of Christian Democrats and held the defence post in the Godmanis cabinet, the first government after Latvia regained its independence.
- President Ulmanis has sent a letter to Prime minister Andris Shkele urging the cabinet to ease the technicalities of the naturalisation procedure.
- Parliament ratified the European Convention for Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms of 1950.
- Parliament passed a new law on real estate tax, to replace the existing land tax and real estate tax in the year 2000.
- A bomb went off in a car in the centre of Riga injuring two.
DIENA
- Diena revealed that President Ulmanis has been violating two articles of the constitution as he did not officially give up posts in private businesses.

- The leader of the newly formed National Party of Reforms, Aleksandrs Kirshteins, announced that small party factions would bloc amendments to the election law, suggested by three major parties and aimed at making it more difficult for small parties to get parliament seats.
- The faction of Latvia's way is discussing ways to ease the procedure of dismissing parliament. Under current legislation, the president can only dismiss parliament after a national referendum.
NEATKARIGA RITA AVIZE
- State revenue service claims that it informed parliament about how the anti-corruption law was being observed by state officials after criticism it failed to monitor the law.

- Most politicians questioned by the paper believe a series of the corruption scandals would not influence the situation in the country: the government won't step down and no early elections will be called.
BIZNES & BALTIYA
- The cabinet decided that Latvia needs a special board to fight corruption.
- Central bank chief Einars Repshe said the amount of lats in circulation in May rose by 10 million lats to 300 million, while the central bank's currency reserves increased by 15 million lats.
DIENAS BIZNESS
- A delegation including 25 German businessmen representing German Machinery and Plant Manufacturing is visiting Latvia seeking potential subcontractors.
-- Riga newsroom, +371 721 5240 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
